title: Unit tensor generators for scalar extension
statement:
Two maps out of an ordinary normalized scalar-extension object agree if they agree on every local tensor 1⊗x. The scalar extension of a module map sends c⊗x to c⊗f(x). These statements apply to arbitrary sheaves of rings and the fixed sheafified tensor models.

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe u v w
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [EssentiallySmall.{w} C]
  {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
  [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
  {R S : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}} {φ : R ⟶ S} (A : SystemScalarModel φ)
theorem systemScalarModel_hom_ext
    (P : ringedSiteModules.{w} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R))
    (M : ringedSiteModules.{w} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S))
    (f g : A.model.E.obj P ⟶ M)
    (h : ∀ U x, f.val.app U (systemModelTmul A.model P U 1 x) =
      g.val.app U (systemModelTmul A.model P U 1 x)) : f = g
```

source.place: Construction 4.1, printed p. 21, ordinary evaluation left extension and the subsequence generalization; Stacks 03DA, 03DB, 06YT and 07D9

proof.text: Apply injectivity of the ordinary tensor-restriction Hom equivalence. Its transpose evaluates x as the map applied to the normalized unit 1⊗x, so the given generator equality makes the transposes equal on all sections. For functoriality use naturality of the unit; scalar linearity supplies the formula for arbitrary c.
